course.programmeTitle: Bachelor of Engineering in Data Science and Engineering
course.title: Math II-Linear Algebra
course.description: Linear Algebra is fundamental to modern engineering, computer science and data science. This course develops conceptual understanding and computational fluency in vectors and matrices, matrix multiplication, Gaussian elimination, vector spaces and subspaces, complete solution to linear equations, independence/basis/dimension, projections and least squares, Gram–Schmidt method, determinant, eigenvalues/eigenvectors, symmetric/positive definite matrices, and singular value decomposition (SVD). Applications include data fitting, image processing, and data-driven modeling with SVD. Teaching and learning follow a flipped-classroom and active learning approach.

clos.description: Apply Gaussian elimination and matrix operations to solve general linear systems
Apply the concepts of basis/dimension, orthogonality, least squares and eigenvalues/eigenvectors, and SVD in addressing data-driven problems
Demonstrate effective communication of linear-algebra reasoning, solutions, and interpretations through oral and written presentations
clos.assessmentMethodsRaw: Project Reports, Project Presentations, Peer evaluation (FA)

clos.description: Use mathematical software (such as Python, Mathematica) under guidance to compute the solution of linear equations, projection vectors, eigenvalues and eigenvectors, and SVD

topics.title: Topic 1: Vectors and Matrices Vectors and Linear Combinations Short Introduction to Matrices Dot product and length of vectors
topics.llosRaw: -LLO1: Explain linear combination of vectors using a matrix operation - LLO2: Explain when two vectors are orthogonal - LLO3: Compute the length of vectors using the concept of dot product

topics.title: Topic 2: Matrix multiplication
topics.llosRaw: - LLO1: Compute matrix multiplication in four different ways - LLO2: Explain the meaning of matrix multiplication intuitively

topics.title: Topic 3: Solving Linear equations using Gaussian Elimination Different pictures of linear equations Gaussian eliminations
topics.llosRaw: - LLO1: Describe system of linear equations in different ways - LLO2: Apply Gaussian elimination to solve a square system of linear equations

topics.title: Topic 4: Vector spaces and subspaces
topics.llosRaw: - LLO1: Describe the concept of a vector space intuitively - LLO2: Identify all subspaces of a vector space

topics.title: Topic 5: Complete solution to Ax=b
topics.llosRaw: - LLO1: Describe the column space and nullspace of a matrix - LLO2: Solve the homogeneous linear equations using nullspace - LLO3: Solve the complete solution of Ax=b

topics.title: Topic 6: Linear Independence, spanning, and bases
topics.llosRaw: - LLO1: Explain the concept of linear independence, spanning, a basis of a vector space - LLO2: Compute the basis of column space and nullspace of a matrix - LLO3: Determine the dimension of column space and nullspace of a matrix

topics.title: Topic 7: Projection and least square method
topics.llosRaw: - LLO1: Compute the projection of a vector onto column space of a matrix - LLO2: Use least square method to solve best approximate solution to inconsistent systems of linear equations

topics.title: Topic 8: Orthogonalization by Gram–Schmidt (A = QR)
topics.llosRaw: - LLO1: Perform Gram–Schmidt method - LLO2: Compute QR decomposition of a matrix

topics.title: Topic 9: Determinant
topics.llosRaw: - LLO1: Explain properties and geometric meaning of determinant - LLO2: Compute the determinant of a matrix

topics.title: Topic 10: Eigenvalues and eigenvectors
topics.llosRaw: -LLO1: Compute eigenvalues/eigenvectors of a matrix -LLO2: diagonalize a matrix using eigen thing

topics.title: Topic 11: Symmetric matrices and positive definite matrices
topics.llosRaw: - LLO1: Analyse symmetric & positive definite matrices; energy & stability

topics.title: Topic 12: Singular Value Decomposition (SVD)
topics.llosRaw: - LLO1: Compute SVD decomposition of a matrix - LLO2: Interpret singular values and vectors

studentResponsibilitiesRaw: Read the learning materials beforehand which means to be ready for the next session. Be completely engaged in class, active, take notes, and ask questions in class. Students are required to participate in various activities in and out of the classroom, such as group work, and individual homework for assignments and reports assigned by the subject teacher. Submit the assigned tasks such as homework, assignments, or research proposal on time.
coursePolicyRaw: Attendance & Preparation Students are expected to attend all classes (online/on-site). Assigned readings and preparation outlines must be completed before class if any. Active participation in group discussions and post-chapter evaluations is required. Academic Integrity All assignments, quizzes, and exams must be done individually. Academic misconduct includes: - Presenting others’ work as one’s own. - Engaging in plagiarism or cheating. Homework & Assignments Preparation outlines must be submitted on time; late submissions incur penalties. Peer discussion is encouraged, but midterm and final exams must be independent. Examinations Midterm and final exams are closed-book. Penalties Violations of academic integrity may result in a failing grade and referral to the Office of Student Affairs. Students uncertain about potential violations should consult the instructor in advance.
